extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on request body — Full remote code execution on the server via a crafted pickle payload (e.g. using `__reduce__`). [verified: raw request body is passed directly to pickle.loads with zero validation, enabling RCE via crafted __reduce__ payload.]

Hardcoded admin credentials — Anyone with source access (or default-credential guessing) can authenticate as admin. [verified: USERNAME/PASSWORD are hardcoded plaintext constants compared directly with no other credential source or hashing.]

SQL Injection via unsanitized id parameter — Attacker can manipulate SQL query logic to exfiltrate, modify, or delete database data (in a real DB backend). [verified: user_id is string-concatenated into a SQL query with no parameterization; though run_query is a stub, the pattern is the injectable sink representing a real DB call.]

Command Injection via unsanitized ping target — Attacker-controlled arguments passed to the system `ping` binary; can inject additional ping flags, cause denial-of-service (flood ping), or exploit any vulnerability in the ping utility's argument parsing. [verified: ip is passed unsanitized as an argv element to ping; no shell but attacker can inject flags like -c or hostnames triggering long-running/flood behavior, and no validation exists anywhere in the file.]

Missing rate limiting on login endpoint — Attacker can brute-force credentials without restriction. [verified: login endpoint has no throttling, lockout, or delay logic anywhere in the file, allowing unlimited brute force attempts.]

Flask debug mode enabled — If reached in a deployed/production-like context, the interactive Werkzeug debugger exposes a console that allows arbitrary code execution, and verbose stack traces leak internals. [verified: app.run(debug=True) is in the __main__ entry point actually executed when the script runs, enabling the Werkzeug debugger/RCE console if reached in a deployed context.]
